headline: The Malay grievance, read structurally: capture, not racial competition.
context: The Third Malaysia Plan gave the NEP two prongs: eradicating poverty irrespective of race, and restructuring society. The 13MP (2026-2030) pairs targeted subsidies with an intensified Bumiputera empowerment agenda.

changes.summary: Correction: Replaced the Kuala Lumpur to Sabah income-gap ratio with KL's median household income of RM10,805, and stated the national poverty rate as 5.1%.

cards.big: The Third Malaysia Plan set two NEP prongs: ending poverty 'irrespective of race' and restructuring society. The World Bank finds most inequality lies within ethnic groups.
cards.sub: World Bank (Feb 2025): in 2022, 87% of income inequality came from differences within ethnic groups; 13% from gaps between them.

cards.big: Parliament passed the Government Procurement Bill 2025. Clause 35 makes it an offence to transfer or novate a government contract without approval.
cards.sub: Malay Mail reported the law aims to end the 'Ali Baba' contract culture of fronting. No official leakage figure is public.

cards.big: IDEAS counted 238 political appointments to GLC and statutory body boards under the Anwar administration up to October 2025.
cards.sub: IDEAS also found 78% of chair roles at the 135 federal statutory bodies it reviewed lack clearly defined qualification criteria.

cards.big: DOSM 2024: income Gini 0.390; the Chinese ethnic group has the highest internal inequality (0.412). The World Bank calls East Malaysian Bumiputera the most disadvantaged.
cards.sub: DOSM: Sabah's poverty rate was 17.7% in 2024, more than triple the national 5.1%.

cards.big: Most income inequality sits within ethnic groups. The World Bank's test for ethnicity-based policy: does it reach disadvantaged Bumiputera, or those already succeeding?
A B40 sub-quota inside the Bumi quota. An independent appointments commissioner. Workforce-verified procurement audits. Pro-Malay reform that doesn't dismantle Article 153.
